issues.description: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() is specified as returning void in the UML in problem_statement.md, but the reference solution implements it as `public boolean checkOrderReady()` and returns a boolean. This creates a signature inconsistency that can cause student implementations to fail compilation against tests/UML expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across all artifacts: change the solution (and expected student API/tests) to `public void checkOrderReady()` with no return value, or update the UML/problem statement (and any tests) to specify `boolean checkOrderReady()`.

issues.description: The shared stock is implemented with a static getter `public static Stock getStock()` in the solution, but the provided Main example code calls it as an instance method (`shop.getStock()`). This inconsistency in how students are shown to access stock (static vs instance access) can be confusing and may lead to compilation errors if students follow the example but implement a different getter form.
issues.suggestedFix: Make usage consistent: either update Main to call `SealSaloon.getStock()` everywhere (static access), or add a non-static `public Stock getStock()` instance method (returning the shared static stock) and keep the example instance-based.
